---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/hedgedoc/hedgedoc
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: quay.io/hedgedoc/hedgedoc:1.11.1
  port: 3000
  vm: m1.small
  flavor_id: "2"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0348
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: hedgedoc
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ DEPLOY 1.11.1, NOT THE DEFAULT BRANCH. hedgedoc/hedgedoc's default branch is `develop`, which is HedgeDoc 2.0.0-ALPHA, and every automatic tool lands there first. That branch's docker/docker-compose.yml is a four-service stack (backend, frontend, postgres, and a Caddy publishing 80, 443 and 443/udp), it configures everything with an HD_* prefix instead of CMD_*, and it pins images to `:develop`, a moving tag. docs/content/files/setup-docker/docker-compose.yml on the same branch pins 2.0.0-alpha.3. On redu the Caddy alone is wrong, because redu already terminates TLS at its own edge. The newest RELEASE is 1.11.1 (2026-07-24): one container, CMD_* environment, and the compose shape below, which comes from upstream's own hedgedoc/container repo."
  - "⛔ THE IMAGE IS ON QUAY.IO, AND DOCKER HUB DOES NOT HAVE IT. Checked on 2026-08-17: the Docker Hub API returns \"object not found\" for hedgedoc/hedgedoc, so a habit-written hedgedoc/hedgedoc:1.11.1 simply does not resolve. Use quay.io/hedgedoc/hedgedoc:1.11.1 (published 2026-07-24, sha256:«REDACTED:longhex:96aa6735»). The bare 1.11.1, 1.11.1-debian, debian and latest tags all carry that same digest; 1.11.1-alpine is a genuinely different image. Pin the version either way."
  - "⛔⛔ SET CMD_SESSION_SECRET, OR EVERY REDEPLOY LOGS EVERYONE OUT AND NOTHING ERRORS. lib/config/default.js:63 ships sessionSecret as the literal string 'secret', and lib/config/index.js:164-170 detects that exact value and substitutes a RANDOM 128-character secret at every boot, logging a warning whose own words are 'All users will be logged out.' A warning in a log nobody reads is not a failure anyone notices. Generate one long alphanumeric value, pass it as CMD_SESSION_SECRET, and REUSE THE SAME VALUE on every redeploy. Keep it out of this file and out of the deploy log: hand it to the user in the session."
  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN: NOBODY, EVER. HedgeDoc 1.x HAS NO ADMINISTRATOR ROLE AND NO ADMIN PANEL. There is no admin router in lib/web at 1.11.1 (the routers are baseRouter, statusRouter, auth, historyRouter, userRouter, imageRouter and note/router), no first-user-is-owner branch, and nothing to claim. Every account is an ordinary account; a NOTE has an owner, an instance does not. So there is no ownership race to lose, and correspondingly no way to lock the instance down after the fact from inside the app. Everything below is therefore configuration you set BEFORE the hostname is reachable, because there is no UI that can fix it afterwards."
  - "⛔⛔ AN ANONYMOUS VISITOR'S NOTE IS WORLD-EDITABLE, AND THIS IS THE ONE NO TUTORIAL MENTIONS. lib/config/default.js:37 ships allowAnonymous TRUE, so anyone who finds the URL can create notes on your VM without an account. Then lib/models/note.js:113-118: when a note is created with NO owner, its permission is NOT your configured default, it is `freely`, and lib/realtime.js:641-644 says `freely` blocks nobody. So an anonymous note on a stock instance can be read AND edited by any other stranger who has the link. Ship CMD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=false from the first boot. Note that upstream's own config.json.example agrees: its `production` block sets allowAnonymous to false (config.json.example:37-39), which is the opposite of the code default."
  - "⛔ REGISTRATION IS OPEN ON FIRST BOOT: CLOSE IT WITH CMD_ALLOW_EMAIL_REGISTER=false. lib/config/default.js:176,177 ship email TRUE and allowEmailRegister TRUE, so /register is live the moment the hostname resolves and anyone can make an account on hardware you pay for. The mechanism is unusually clean to verify: lib/web/auth/email/index.js:40 only REGISTERS the POST /register route when allowEmailRegister is true, so with it false the route does not exist and Express answers 404. ⚠️ Check the POLARITY: 404 is the PASS here, and 400 (the route exists and rejected your empty body) is the FAIL."
  - "HOW YOU THEN GET AN ACCOUNT, WITH REGISTRATION CLOSED. Sign-IN still works with CMD_EMAIL left at its default true; only the register route goes away. Create your user inside the container with upstream's own tool: bin/manage_users, whose usage line is `bin/manage_users [--pass password] (--add | --del) user-email` and which also takes --reset. ⚠️ Run it INTERACTIVELY (docker exec -it, no --pass) so it prompts with the echo hidden: an argument passed on the command line is visible in `ps` to every user on that machine, and it lands in your shell history. Do the same for --reset."
  - "⛔ CMD_URL_ADDPORT MUST BE false AND CMD_PROTOCOL_USESSL MUST BE true, AND UPSTREAM'S COMPOSE SHIPS THE OPPOSITE OF BOTH. lib/config/buildDomainOriginWithProtocol.js:5-17 builds every generated link from domain, protocolUseSSL and urlAddPort, and with urlAddPort true and the container listening on 3000 you get https://your-host:3000 on an edge that only serves 443. That serverURL is used for redirects after sign-in, for OAuth callbacks, and for the URL of a note you just created (lib/web/note/util.js:93), so it fails in the browser rather than in the log. Upstream's compose sets CMD_URL_ADDPORT=true and CMD_PROTOCOL_USESSL=false because it assumes you hit the container directly on port 3000. On redu, invert both. CMD_DOMAIN is the BARE HOSTNAME, no scheme and no path, exactly as upstream's compose comment says, so generate the dname yourself up front in the full <label>-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud form and pass just that."
  - "⛔ DATABASE: pass CMD_DB_URL or the container will NOT START, and that is the good news. lib/models/index.js:24-27 hands the URL straight to Sequelize 5.22.5, whose constructor THROWS 'Dialect needs to be explicitly supplied as of v4.0.0' when neither a URL nor a dialect is given (sequelize lib/sequelize.js:274-276). So unlike most apps in this library there is no silent SQLite fallback by OMISSION. The trap is by COPY-PASTE: sqlite3 is bundled in the image and upstream's own compose comments offer `CMD_DB_URL=sqlite:///data/sqlite.db (NOT RECOMMENDED)`, which comes up perfectly healthy and takes every note with it on the next redeploy. redu injects a variable called literally DATABASE_URL in postgresql:// form, and Sequelize parses that scheme and normalises it to the postgres dialect (sequelize lib/sequelize.js:189,278), so the wiring is CMD_DB_URL: \"${DATABASE_URL}\" with no name mapping to get wrong. deploy_compose only APPENDS to the project .env, it never edits your compose, so the compose must interpolate it itself."
  - "PROVE THE DATABASE WIRING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, BECAUSE AN ABSENCE ALONE PROVES NOTHING. Run `sudo docker exec <container> printenv CMD_DB_URL` and confirm it names the private database VM: that is the positive half, and it is also what tells you your exec command worked at all. THEN `sudo docker exec <container> ls -la /hedgedoc` and confirm there is no *.sqlite file. If the first command errors, the second one's empty output means nothing. Recent deploys in this library found docker on the VM rather than podman; if the binary is missing, do not read the empty output as a pass."
  - "SSL TO THE DATABASE IS A DELIBERATE CHOICE HERE, NOT A DEFAULT. redu's injected DATABASE_URL carries no query string, and this driver is node-postgres through Sequelize rather than libpq, so there is no sslmode=prefer to fall back on. Sequelize 5 does pass a URL's query string through to the driver as dialectOptions (lib/sequelize.js:215-222), so that is where you would add it. Over redu's private network plaintext is survivable; say in the handover which you chose rather than leaving it unstated."
  - "ONE DATABASE, NO SUPERUSER, NO migrate_command. Audited every file under lib/migrations at 1.11.1: 21 migrations, 6 createTable calls (the control that proves the grep worked) and ZERO CREATE EXTENSION, CREATE DATABASE or CREATE SCHEMA. So this app never hits redu's one-database-per-managed-Postgres limit and db_superuser is not needed. app.js:309-313 runs the migrations itself at boot, before it starts listening, which is also why /_health answering {\"ready\":true} is a strong signal rather than a cosmetic one."
  - "⛔ MOUNT A VOLUME ON /hedgedoc/public/uploads. Image uploads default to the filesystem backend (lib/config/default.js:74-75, uploadsPath ./public/uploads at :60), so every image pasted into a note lands inside the container. Postgres holds the notes; the images embedded in them do not live there. Upstream's entrypoint prints a large WARNING banner when that path is not a mountpoint (resources/docker-entrypoint.sh:12-27) and chowns it to the hedgedoc user when the container starts as root (:30-35), so a named volume is the simple correct answer. With CMD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=false and CMD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_EDITS=false, HedgeDoc automatically resolves enableUploads to 'registered' (lib/config/index.js:82-88), which is what you want: leave CMD_ENABLE_UPLOADS unset and let it derive."
  - "DECIDE WHO CAN READ A NOTE, BECAUSE 'editable' DOES NOT MEAN PRIVATE. lib/web/note/util.js:43-51: a note whose permission is private is owner-only, limited or protected requires ANY signed-in user, and everything else, including the default 'editable', is readable by ANYONE holding the link, signed in or not. lib/realtime.js:641-655 is the matching write rule: 'editable' lets any signed-in user edit. The note ids are random, so this is obscurity rather than access control. If the user wants a team wiki whose links are useless to outsiders, set CMD_DEFAULT_PERMISSION=limited and say so; if they want shareable read-only links, leave it. Make it a decision, not an inheritance."
  - "TURN OFF THE STATS API. lib/config/default.js:194 ships enableStatsApi TRUE, and lib/web/statusRouter.js:22-33 serves /status to anyone when it is on, reporting the instance's note and user counts. Upstream's own production example turns it off (config.json.example:39). Set CMD_ENABLE_STATS_API=false unless the user wants it. /_health stays available either way, which is what redu's health probe and the container's own HEALTHCHECK use."
  - "PORT 3000, AND THE HEALTH ENDPOINT IS /_health. alpine/Dockerfile:79 exposes 3000 and its HEALTHCHECK runs resources/healthcheck.mjs, which fetches /_health and requires the JSON field `ready` to be truthy. Pass port 3000 to deploy_compose. Socket.io rides the same port and redu creates every proxy host with websocket upgrades allowed, so live collaboration works over the public hostname with nothing extra."
  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO REQUIREMENT IN PROSE. The closest thing to a figure anywhere is the commented-out `mem_limit: 256mb` on the app service in upstream's own hedgedoc/container docker-compose.yml, which is a maintainer's hint and not a measurement. m1.small (1 vCPU / 2 GB) is reasoning from 'a Node/Express app with socket.io and no run-time build step'. The thing that would actually move it is concurrent editing, because HedgeDoc holds each open note in memory while people are connected to it (lib/realtime.js). Real-time collaborative markdown notes, on your own machine, in the EU: one small Node container, a
managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL your team can edit together in the browser.

## What this deploys

- **HedgeDoc 1.11.1** from the official image on quay.io, pinned, on one m1.small VM, port 3000.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so notes and accounts survive every redeploy.
- A volume on `/hedgedoc/public/uploads`, which holds every image pasted into a note.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS, with websocket upgrades allowed so live
  collaboration works.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## Deploy the release, not the default branch

The repository's default branch is `develop`, and that is HedgeDoc **2.0.0-alpha**: four
services, a bundled Caddy that wants ports 80 and 443, a different configuration prefix, and
images on a moving `:develop` tag. Any tool that clones the repo and looks for a compose file
lands there. The newest actual release is **1.11.1**, it is one container, and the compose below is
upstream's own from the `hedgedoc/container` repo with its bundled Postgres removed.

## The compose

```yaml
services:
  hedgedoc:
    image: quay.io/hedgedoc/hedgedoc:1.11.1
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      CMD_DB_URL: "${DATABASE_URL}"
      CMD_DOMAIN: "${HEDGEDOC_HOST}"
      CMD_PROTOCOL_USESSL: "true"
      CMD_URL_ADDPORT: "false"
      CMD_SESSION_SECRET: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      CMD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS: "false"
      CMD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_EDITS: "false"
      CMD_ALLOW_EMAIL_REGISTER: "false"
      CMD_ALLOW_FREEURL: "false"
      CMD_ENABLE_STATS_API: "false"
      CMD_IMAGE_UPLOAD_TYPE: "filesystem"
    volumes:
      - hedgedoc-uploads:/hedgedoc/public/uploads
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
volumes:
  hedgedoc-uploads:
```

`HEDGEDOC_HOST` is the **bare hostname**, no scheme and no trailing slash, from a dname you
generate before deploying. `DATABASE_URL` is injected by redu. `HEDGEDOC_SESSION_SECRET` is
yours to generate, and you must reuse the same value on every redeploy.

## The three that actually break it

**The session secret.** Left unset, HedgeDoc generates a random one at every boot and only writes
a warning to the log. Nothing fails. Everyone is simply logged out again after each redeploy.

**Anonymous notes.** `allowAnonymous` ships **true**, and a note created without an owner is
given the `freely` permission rather than your configured default, which means any stranger with
the link can edit it. The recipe closes anonymous access before the hostname is reachable.

**The URL settings.** Upstream's compose sets `CMD_URL_ADDPORT=true` and
`CMD_PROTOCOL_USESSL=false`, because it assumes you reach the container directly on port 3000.
Behind redu's TLS edge both are wrong, and the symptom is that sign-in redirects and freshly
created note links point at `https://your-host:3000`, which nothing serves.

## Creating your account, with registration closed

```bash

# reaches your shell history or the process list that every user on the machine can read.
sudo docker exec -it "$(sudo docker ps --filter name=hedgedoc -q | head -1)" \
  bin/manage_users --add you@example.org
```

Then sign in normally. Sign-in stays enabled; only the register route is removed.

## Proving it is actually closed

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove this HedgeDoc is not handing accounts, or world-editable notes, to strangers.
#   ./verify-hedgedoc.sh hedgedoc-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = closed, 1 = OPEN (fix it now), 2 = inconclusive (it may still be starting).
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-hedgedoc.sh <host>}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
rc=0

# 1. GATE. /_health only answers once HedgeDoc is listening, and it only listens after Sequelize
#    authenticated and the migrations ran (app.js:309-313). So a ready:true here proves the app AND
#    the managed Postgres. Without this gate every assertion below is vacuous, because redu's edge
#    answers 502 from openresty while the container starts.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/health" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/_health")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /_health answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
  [ "$code" = "502" ] && echo "  502 is redu's edge while the container starts. Wait, re-run." >&2
  exit 2
fi
if ! grep -q '"ready":true' "$TMP/health"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /_health answered 200 but not ready:true." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK: HedgeDoc is serving and reached its database."

# 2. POSITIVE CONTROL FOR THE NEXT CHECK. POST /login with an empty body must answer 400, which
#    proves the e-mail auth router is mounted. Without this, a 404 on /register would be
#    ambiguous: it could mean registration is closed, or that e-mail auth is off entirely.
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data '' "https://$HOST/login")
if [ "$code" != "400" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: POST /login answered $code, expected 400 for an empty body." >&2
  echo "  The route table is not what this script was written against; prove it another way." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK: the e-mail auth router is mounted (so the next check means something)."

# 3. THE REGISTRATION ASSERTION, on the route table rather than on a flag. HedgeDoc only registers
#    POST /register when allowEmailRegister is true, so 404 is the PASS and 400 is the failure.
#    An empty body is sent deliberately: if the route DOES exist, nothing is created.
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data '' "https://$HOST/register")
case "$code" in
  404) echo "OK: registration is closed (the route does not exist)." ;;
  400|302|200)
    echo "FAIL: registration is OPEN. POST /register answered $code, so the route exists." >&2
    echo "  Anyone who finds this URL can create an account on your VM." >&2
    echo "  Redeploy with CMD_ALLOW_EMAIL_REGISTER=false." >&2
    rc=1 ;;
  *)
    echo "INCONCLUSIVE: POST /register answered $code, which this script does not recognise." >&2
    exit 2 ;;
esac

# 4. THE ANONYMOUS ASSERTION. ⚠️ POLARITY WARNING: HedgeDoc does NOT answer 403 here. For an
#    anonymous request errorForbidden REDIRECTS to serverURL (lib/errors.js:4-16), and an allowed
#    anonymous request ALSO redirects, to the new note. Both are 302; only the target differs.
#    This same check therefore doubles as a test of CMD_PROTOCOL_USESSL and CMD_URL_ADDPORT.
loc=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{redirect_url}' "https://$HOST/new")
case "$loc" in
  "")
    echo "INCONCLUSIVE: GET /new did not redirect at all. Expected a 302." >&2
    exit 2 ;;
  "https://$HOST/")
    echo "OK: anonymous note creation is refused, and the generated URLs are correct." ;;
  *":3000"*)
    echo "FAIL: generated URLs carry the container port ($loc)." >&2
    echo "  Set CMD_URL_ADDPORT=false. Sign-in redirects and note links are broken until you do." >&2
    rc=1 ;;
  "http://"*)
    echo "FAIL: generated URLs are http, not https ($loc)." >&2
    echo "  Set CMD_PROTOCOL_USESSL=true. redu terminates TLS at its edge." >&2
    rc=1 ;;
  "https://$HOST/"*)
    echo "FAIL: anonymous note creation is OPEN. GET /new created a note at $loc," >&2
    echo "  and a note with no owner is given the 'freely' permission, so any stranger with the" >&2
    echo "  link can edit it. Redeploy with CMD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=false and delete that note." >&2
    rc=1 ;;
  *)
    echo "INCONCLUSIVE: GET /new redirected to $loc, which this script does not recognise." >&2
    exit 2 ;;
esac

# 5. LIMITATION, stated rather than hidden: if CMD_DOMAIN never reached the container, serverURL is
#    the empty string and HedgeDoc redirects to a RELATIVE '/', which curl resolves against this
#    host and which therefore looks identical to the good case above. HedgeDoc logs a warning for
#    it at boot ("Neither 'domain' nor 'CMD_DOMAIN' is configured"), so confirm directly:
echo "Now confirm CMD_DOMAIN took, which this script cannot see from the outside:"
echo "  sudo docker exec <container> printenv CMD_DOMAIN CMD_PROTOCOL_USESSL CMD_URL_ADDPORT"

exit "$rc"
```

## What an anonymous request can reach

With this recipe's settings: the sign-in page, `/_health`, and any note whose permission leaves it
readable. Note creation is refused, registration is refused, and `/status` is refused because the
stats API is off. On the **stock** settings, by contrast, an anonymous visitor can create notes,
and those notes are editable by any other anonymous visitor holding the link.

Note ids are random, so a readable note is protected by obscurity rather than by access control. If
that is not good enough for the user's content, set `CMD_DEFAULT_PERMISSION=limited` so a note
requires a signed-in account to open at all.

      CMD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS: "false"
      CMD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_EDITS: "false"
      CMD_ALLOW_EMAIL_REGISTER: "false"
      CMD_ALLOW_FREEURL: "false"
      CMD_ENABLE_STATS_API: "false"
      CMD_IMAGE_UPLOAD_TYPE: "filesystem"

    ports:

```

`HEDGEDOC_HOST` is the **bare hostname**, no scheme and no trailing slash, from a dname you
generate before deploying. `DATABASE_URL` is injected by redu. `HEDGEDOC_SESSION_SECRET` is
yours to generate, and you must reuse the same value on every redeploy.

## The three that actually break it

**The session secret.** Left unset, HedgeDoc generates a random one at every boot and only writes
a warning to the log. Nothing fails. Everyone is simply logged out again after each redeploy.

**Anonymous notes.** `allowAnonymous` ships **true**, and a note created without an owner is
given the `freely` permission rather than your configured default, which means any stranger with
the link can edit it. The recipe closes anonymous access before the hostname is reachable.

**The URL settings.** Upstream's compose sets `CMD_URL_ADDPORT=true` and
`CMD_PROTOCOL_USESSL=false`, because it assumes you reach the container directly on port 3000.
Behind redu's TLS edge both are wrong, and the symptom is that sign-in redirects and freshly
created note links point at `https://your-host:3000`, which nothing serves.

## Creating your account, with registration closed

```bash
# Interactive on purpose: it prompts for the password with the echo hidden, so the value never
# reaches your shell history or the process list that every user on the machine can read.
sudo docker exec -it "$(sudo docker ps --filter name=hedgedoc -q | head -1)" \
  bin/manage_users --add you@example.org
```

Then sign in normally. Sign-in stays enabled; only the register route is removed.

## Proving it is actually closed

Run this once the deploy reports ready.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove this HedgeDoc is not handing accounts, or world-editable notes, to strangers.
#   ./verify-hedgedoc.sh hedgedoc-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = closed, 1 = OPEN (fix it now), 2 = inconclusive (it may still be starting).
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-hedgedoc.sh <host>}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
rc=0

# 1. GATE. /_health only answers once HedgeDoc is listening, and it only listens after Sequelize
#    authenticated and the migrations ran (app.js:309-313). So a ready:true here proves the app AND
#    the managed Postgres. Without this gate every assertion below is vacuous, because redu's edge
#    answers 502 from openresty while the container starts.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/health" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/_health")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /_health answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
  [ "$code" = "502" ] && echo "  502 is redu's edge while the container starts. Wait, re-run." >&2
  exit 2
fi
if ! grep -q '"ready":true' "$TMP/health"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /_health answered 200 but not ready:true." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK: HedgeDoc is serving and reached its database."

# 2. POSITIVE CONTROL FOR THE NEXT CHECK. POST /login with an empty body must answer 400, which
#    proves the e-mail auth router is mounted. Without this, a 404 on /register would be
#    ambiguous: it could mean registration is closed, or that e-mail auth is off entirely.
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data '' "https://$HOST/login")
if [ "$code" != "400" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: POST /login answered $code, expected 400 for an empty body." >&2
  echo "  The route table is not what this script was written against; prove it another way." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK: the e-mail auth router is mounted (so the next check means something)."

# 3. THE REGISTRATION ASSERTION, on the route table rather than on a flag. HedgeDoc only registers
#    POST /register when allowEmailRegister is true, so 404 is the PASS and 400 is the failure.
#    An empty body is sent deliberately: if the route DOES exist, nothing is created.
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data '' "https://$HOST/register")
case "$code" in
  404) echo "OK: registration is closed (the route does not exist)." ;;
  400|302|200)
    echo "FAIL: registration is OPEN. POST /register answered $code, so the route exists." >&2
    echo "  Anyone who finds this URL can create an account on your VM." >&2
    echo "  Redeploy with CMD_ALLOW_EMAIL_REGISTER=false." >&2
    rc=1 ;;
  *)
    echo "INCONCLUSIVE: POST /register answered $code, which this script does not recognise." >&2
    exit 2 ;;
esac

# 4. THE ANONYMOUS ASSERTION. ⚠️ POLARITY WARNING: HedgeDoc does NOT answer 403 here. For an
#    anonymous request errorForbidden REDIRECTS to serverURL (lib/errors.js:4-16), and an allowed
#    anonymous request ALSO redirects, to the new note. Both are 302; only the target differs.
#    This same check therefore doubles as a test of CMD_PROTOCOL_USESSL and CMD_URL_ADDPORT.
loc=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{redirect_url}' "https://$HOST/new")
case "$loc" in
  "")
    echo "INCONCLUSIVE: GET /new did not redirect at all. Expected a 302." >&2
    exit 2 ;;
  "https://$HOST/")
    echo "OK: anonymous note creation is refused, and the generated URLs are correct." ;;
  *":3000"*)
    echo "FAIL: generated URLs carry the container port ($loc)." >&2
    echo "  Set CMD_URL_ADDPORT=false. Sign-in redirects and note links are broken until you do." >&2
    rc=1 ;;
  "http://"*)
    echo "FAIL: generated URLs are http, not https ($loc)." >&2
    echo "  Set CMD_PROTOCOL_USESSL=true. redu terminates TLS at its edge." >&2
    rc=1 ;;
  "https://$HOST/"*)
    echo "FAIL: anonymous note creation is OPEN. GET /new created a note at $loc," >&2
    echo "  and a note with no owner is given the 'freely' permission, so any stranger with the" >&2
    echo "  link can edit it. Redeploy with CMD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=false and delete that note." >&2
    rc=1 ;;
  *)
    echo "INCONCLUSIVE: GET /new redirected to $loc, which this script does not recognise." >&2
    exit 2 ;;
esac

# 5. LIMITATION, stated rather than hidden: if CMD_DOMAIN never reached the container, serverURL is
#    the empty string and HedgeDoc redirects to a RELATIVE '/', which curl resolves against this
#    host and which therefore looks identical to the good case above. HedgeDoc logs a warning for
#    it at boot ("Neither 'domain' nor 'CMD_DOMAIN' is configured"), so confirm directly:
echo "Now confirm CMD_DOMAIN took, which this script cannot see from the outside:"
echo "  sudo docker exec <container> printenv CMD_DOMAIN CMD_PROTOCOL_USESSL CMD_URL_ADDPORT"

exit "$rc"
```

## What an anonymous request can reach

With this recipe's settings: the sign-in page, `/_health`, and any note whose permission leaves it
readable. Note creation is refused, registration is refused, and `/status` is refused because the
stats API is off. On the **stock** settings, by contrast, an anonymous visitor can create notes,
and those notes are editable by any other anonymous visitor holding the link.

Note ids are random, so a readable note is protected by obscurity rather than by access control. If
that is not good enough for the user's content, set `CMD_DEFAULT_PERMISSION=limited` so a note
requires a signed-in account to open at all.

unchanged, for yourself and your team, triggers nothing extra.

cat > verify-hedgedoc.sh <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove this HedgeDoc is not handing accounts, or world-editable notes, to strangers.
#   ./verify-hedgedoc.sh hedgedoc-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = closed, 1 = OPEN (fix it now), 2 = inconclusive (it may still be starting).
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-hedgedoc.sh <host>}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
rc=0

# 1. GATE. /_health only answers once HedgeDoc is listening, and it only listens after Sequelize
#    authenticated and the migrations ran (app.js:309-313). So a ready:true here proves the app AND
#    the managed Postgres. Without this gate every assertion below is vacuous, because redu's edge
#    answers 502 from openresty while the container starts.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/health" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/_health")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /_health answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
  [ "$code" = "502" ] && echo "  502 is redu's edge while the container starts. Wait, re-run." >&2
  exit 2
fi
if ! grep -q '"ready":true' "$TMP/health"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /_health answered 200 but not ready:true." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK: HedgeDoc is serving and reached its database."

# 2. POSITIVE CONTROL FOR THE NEXT CHECK. POST /login with an empty body must answer 400, which
#    proves the e-mail auth router is mounted. Without this, a 404 on /register would be
#    ambiguous: it could mean registration is closed, or that e-mail auth is off entirely.
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data '' "https://$HOST/login")
if [ "$code" != "400" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: POST /login answered $code, expected 400 for an empty body." >&2
  echo "  The route table is not what this script was written against; prove it another way." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK: the e-mail auth router is mounted (so the next check means something)."

# 3. THE REGISTRATION ASSERTION, on the route table rather than on a flag. HedgeDoc only registers
#    POST /register when allowEmailRegister is true, so 404 is the PASS and 400 is the failure.
#    An empty body is sent deliberately: if the route DOES exist, nothing is created.
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
  -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data '' "https://$HOST/register")
case "$code" in
  404) echo "OK: registration is closed (the route does not exist)." ;;
  400|302|200)
    echo "FAIL: registration is OPEN. POST /register answered $code, so the route exists." >&2
    echo "  Anyone who finds this URL can create an account on your VM." >&2
    echo "  Redeploy with CMD_ALLOW_EMAIL_REGISTER=false." >&2
    rc=1 ;;
  *)
    echo "INCONCLUSIVE: POST /register answered $code, which this script does not recognise." >&2
    exit 2 ;;
esac

# 4. THE ANONYMOUS ASSERTION. POLARITY WARNING: HedgeDoc does NOT answer 403 here. For an
#    anonymous request errorForbidden REDIRECTS to serverURL (lib/errors.js:4-16), and an allowed
#    anonymous request ALSO redirects, to the new note. Both are 302; only the target differs.
#    This same check therefore doubles as a test of CMD_PROTOCOL_USESSL and CMD_URL_ADDPORT.
loc=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{redirect_url}' "https://$HOST/new")
case "$loc" in
  "")
    echo "INCONCLUSIVE: GET /new did not redirect at all. Expected a 302." >&2
    exit 2 ;;
  "https://$HOST/")
    echo "OK: anonymous note creation is refused, and the generated URLs are correct." ;;
  *":3000"*)
    echo "FAIL: generated URLs carry the container port ($loc)." >&2
    echo "  Set CMD_URL_ADDPORT=false. Sign-in redirects and note links are broken until you do." >&2
    rc=1 ;;
  "http://"*)
    echo "FAIL: generated URLs are http, not https ($loc)." >&2
    echo "  Set CMD_PROTOCOL_USESSL=true. redu terminates TLS at its edge." >&2
    rc=1 ;;
  "https://$HOST/"*)
    echo "FAIL: anonymous note creation is OPEN. GET /new created a note at $loc," >&2
    echo "  and a note with no owner is given the 'freely' permission, so any stranger with the" >&2
    echo "  link can edit it. Redeploy with CMD_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=false and delete that note." >&2
    rc=1 ;;
  *)
    echo "INCONCLUSIVE: GET /new redirected to $loc, which this script does not recognise." >&2
    exit 2 ;;
esac

# 5. LIMITATION, stated rather than hidden: if CMD_DOMAIN never reached the container, serverURL is
#    the empty string and HedgeDoc redirects to a RELATIVE '/', which curl resolves against this
#    host and which therefore looks identical to the good case above. HedgeDoc logs a warning for
#    it at boot ("Neither 'domain' nor 'CMD_DOMAIN' is configured"), so confirm directly:
echo "Now confirm CMD_DOMAIN took, which this script cannot see from the outside:"
echo "  sudo docker exec <container> printenv CMD_DOMAIN CMD_PROTOCOL_USESSL CMD_URL_ADDPORT"

exit "$rc"
SH
